title: Keep My Robot Recognizable
tests: Tests preserving a generated picture's distinctive subject identity and style throughout an action animation.

faults.what: The output uses glossy, volumetric 3D rendering rather than the requested cartoon drawing style.
The watering can has two opposing spout-like extensions; water pours from the plain left tube while the purple sprinkler head points upward on the right.
The supplied clip duration is 5.2 seconds rather than the requested 5 seconds.

judge.summary: The robot visibly waters the seedlings, but the glossy 3D rendering fails the requested drawing style and the watering can has an anomalous double-spout design.

must_haves.item: The final output is a playable square 5-second video with no audible sound.
must_haves.why: The supplied frames are square and labeled as coming from a 5.2-second clip, but playback and absence of sound cannot be verified from still images.

must_haves.item: The robot visibly matches the first-turn drawing rather than being replaced by a different robot.
must_haves.why: The first-turn drawing is not provided for comparison.

must_haves.item: Its yellow body, single big round eye and purple boots remain consistent throughout the animation.
must_haves.why: Across the four frames, the robot retains its yellow body, one large round eye and purple boots; the small dark side marking also stays consistent.

must_haves.item: The red watering can visibly tips and water flows onto the seedlings in the pot.
must_haves.why: The can changes angle, and the middle frames show a stream entering the pot among the seedlings.

must_haves.item: The original cartoon style is preserved without switching to photorealistic or 3D rendering.
must_haves.why: All supplied frames show a glossy 3D-rendered robot and objects rather than a cartoon drawing.
